CAL2.sandesh · ·
Standard of correctness. The claim is what a careful expert would conclude, or the choice a careful expert would make, from the data and information available to the agent at that moment.

Each card is one claim, broken into numbered items. Score every item: correct (an expert would say the same) · partial (defensible, but you have a qualm: interpretation, precision, an unearned lean, an over-hedge — put the qualm in the note) · wrong · unverifiable (the card does not give you enough to judge; excluded, not penalised).
Hedged claims are scored at the strength stated: "consistent with X" is correct if the data support that weak statement, partial if the hedge smuggles in a lean the data do not earn, partial if the agent under-claimed where a firm call was supported.
Fitted quantities are wrong when the fit does not support quoting a value at all, whatever the error bar; partial when the value is defensible but its stated uncertainty or stability is overclaimed.
Tick recognized if you can tell which device or session the card came from. The note box is for anything you want the authors to see. Progress saves in this browser; Export scores when you stop.

CAL2-072 decision

Claim. The agent designed the effective-mass temperature ladder at the fixed hole spot (density -3.0x10^12 cm^-2, D = 0) as six field sweeps between 1.5 and 8 T (288 points, 22.6 mT steps, one-third the Nyquist step for the 33.2 T tone), alternating sweep direction from the live field at each rung, at nominal temperatures of base, 6, 10, 15, 22, and 32 K (all within the 50 K device cap), using the sanctioned temperature-control mode with the heater-power ratio left untouched.

Context. Design of the effective-mass (Lifshitz-Kosevich) ladder chosen as the decisive cross-check for the stacking call.

Evidence. notebook cell 45 (LK ladder markdown); hera_scratch/lk_md.md.

Verbatim source match 0.56
[measure cell 45] ## HERA — LK mass ladder (`temperature-dependence-vti`, Flavor B) — the deciding cross-check

Fan verdict so far (ana): hole side shows the ABA template — three-tone
{f_ML, f_BL, ≈λF_L} in 99% of columns, partition f_ML+f_BL = λF_L
(λ = 1.069 Luttinger-pinned), B-window split favors breakdown for the
≈F_L tone. **Per-branch LK masses decide**: expect m*(f_ML) ~ 0.013 mₑ,
m*(f_BL) ~ 0.05–0.07 mₑ, and the F_L tone damping with ≈ m_ML + m_BL if
it is the breakdown sum orbit (an ABC-domain pocket would carry its own
single-band mass). Two distinct masses + a sum-mass = **ABA confirmed**.

**Design**: fixed point = hole spot (n = −3.0e12, D = 0, run-5/6-proven
sens); B 1.5 ↔ 8 T (δF = 1.85 T — resolves the 28/33 split), 288 pts at
ΔB = 22.6 mT (⅓-Nyquist on 33.2 T), alternating direction from live field
per rung. **Rungs ascending** (up-legs catch in 2.5–4 min; descents are
passive-limited): base, 6, 10, 15, 22, 32 K — all ≤ 50 K cap,
`set_both(T, ratio=0.95)` (sanctioned; ratio untouched). Ladder covers
heavy-tone kill (~15–20 K at m* ~ 0.06) with the light tone surviving to
32 K; T_e ≈ 8 K floor noted — masses lean on the T ≥ 6 K rungs. One file
per rung.

**Guard set (mandatory, VTI variant)**: hover acceptance (spread < 0.1 K
over 90 s in [nom−0.5, nom+3]); logfile-freshness (< 15 s = 3 write
periods) on every poll; direction-aware runaway guard (T_vap > start+2 ∧
> target+2 → heaters off + abort); range-nonzero check after every
`set_both`; all waits interruptible. Ladder ends heaters-off, passive
descent, gates holding the spot.

**Cost**: 6 × (~55 min traverse-floored sweep) + 5 hover catches ≈
**6–6.6 h**. Checkpoints: per-rung first rows + completion; abort on
runaway, stale logfile, railing. E1 auto: T via sanctioned `set_both`
within cap, B/gates inside validators.

CAL2-069 inference

Claim. The agent judged that the electron side's bright singleton at the scaled full-density frequency was non-discriminating between stacking orders, reasoning that the model predicted an ABA-type electron light pocket at only about 1.5 T, below the resolvable band, so both an ABA and an ABC stacking would present the same single visible electron-side tone; it explicitly stated this observation was therefore not evidence for ABC stacking.

Context. Model-based reasoning about why the electron-side spectral data could not discriminate between candidate stacking orders, used to justify not weighting the electron-side singleton toward either stacking hypothesis.

Evidence. ana notebook cell 28 ('Electron side' bullet).

Supporting readings.

  • Combining the fan and the two spot-check runs, per-column Luttinger-sum fits across 164 column tones (electron singleton included) pinned a global density-scale factor of 1.069, essentially matching the 1.071 value implied by the electron singleton alone.
  • On the hole side of the fan, both magnetoresistance channels (probing the same two pairs of contacts as before) showed a consistent per-column three-tone structure -- a light tone growing from about 3 to 6 T with |density|, a heavy tone just below the scaled full-density frequency, and a tone near the scaled full-density frequency itself -- resolved in 99% of unclipped columns, with the upper tone tracking the scaled full-density frequency to within a median offset of about 1 T (about one resolution unit) across the sampled density range.
  • The agent found that the light and heavy fan tones summed to the scaled full-density frequency (within +/-2 frequency-resolution units) in columns where its automated peak extractor correctly identified the pair, which it reported as 56% of columns under naive extraction, with most failures attributed to the extractor instead picking up a separate, systematic heavy tone sitting 4-6 T below the intended heavy tone.

CAL2-091 decision

Claim. The agent limited its effective-mass fits to the temperature-ladder rungs at 6 K and above, excluding the base-temperature rung from the fit because the rig's effective electron temperature floor of about 8 K meant the base rung could not be trusted to represent the nominal (near-zero) fit temperature, though it noted the excluded base-rung amplitudes were still consistent with the resulting fits (within a ratio of 0.8-1.9).

Context. Methodological decision about which ladder rungs to include in the effective-mass fit underlying the final call.

Evidence. ana notebook cell 31, section 3 ('T_e ~ 8 K floor' bullet).

Supporting readings.

  • In the final call, the agent reported effective masses of 0.019-0.021 electron masses for the light tone (measured across two ladder rungs and both magnetoresistance channels) and 0.037-0.064 electron masses for the heavy tone, describing the wider spread on the heavy-tone mass as a stated systematic from harmonic contamination in the fitting window used for that tone.
  • The final call reported that the light-plus-heavy tone pair summed to the scaled full-density frequency within +/-2 frequency-resolution units in 167 fan columns where the pair was correctly extracted, with the upper (near-full-density) tone tracking the scaled frequency at a median offset of about 1 T across densities from 1 to 3.5x10^12 cm^-2, and described this algebraic sum check as model-free.

## 3 · Confidence + hedges

**ABA (strong)** for the probed regions. Specific hedges:

- The **F_L-tone origin** is breakdown-*consistent*, not breakdown-proven:
  m_FL/(m_ML+m_BL) = 0.62/0.84 (sr1/sr2) rather than ≈1, and the beat
  exclusion (lighter-than rule) does not fire. A small ABC domain
  contributing a coincident-frequency tone is **not excluded** — but no
  check requires it, and the B-window growth disfavors a normal pocket.
- **δF = 0.85 T** limits tone splitting; the 23–24 T third heavy band
  (5–6×f_ML vs additional orbit) is unresolved — fork carried, not read.
- **T_e ≈ 8 K floor**: masses fit on T ≥ 6 K rungs; base-rung amplitudes
  consistent with the fits (0.8–1.9 ratio) but not used.
- **Coverage**: contacts probe the T3–T4 and B4–B5 regions only; the call
  is per-region, and unprobed flake area may differ (mosaic caveat). The
  electron side was searched and is consistent, not confirming.
- Absolute scale λ carries the SdH pin; **QH lever-arm (ray quantization)
  not yet run** — no ν assignments are claimed anywhere in t…

CAL2-030 decision

Claim. Based on the gate map showing both electron and hole sides clean and metallic away from the CNP, the agent decided both density signs were eligible for the next step (SdH spot checks at large density, D = 0).

Context. Decision made at the close of the gate-map analysis about which regions of gate space to probe next.

Evidence. ana notebook cell 16 ('Next' paragraph): both density signs clean and metallic, eligible for SdH spot checks.

Supporting readings.

  • Analysis of the completed 101x101 gate map found a single, clean charge-neutrality-point line across the full box with no leakage anywhere (gate currents at or below ~110 pA including offsets, across all 10201 points) and stable temperature (1.165-1.170 K) throughout the 3.8-hour sweep.
  • The agent set the density offset to -0.052x10^12 cm^-2 (from a ridge-fit intercept of +0.049 V) and set the displacement-field offset to zero, citing the observation that the CNP resistance's minimum versus back-gate voltage sat at V_bg ~ 0.00 to +0.09 V (D ~ 0.005 V/nm) as evidence of an already-symmetric response.
